param.name: %1 AUTOZERO
param.desc: Enable/disable the weld head's travel axis auto zero feature where the axis will zero itself before a weld. %1 = TRAVEL NAME

param.name: DOWNSLOPE TIME
param.desc: The duration in seconds, beginning when the weld sequence has finished the final segment, during which the weld current will decrease linearly from the programmed PRI AMP/BKG AMP values to the FINAL AMPS value. The DOWN SLOPE period is used to "tie out" the end of the weld neatly.

param.name: %1 START DELAY
param.desc: The duration in seconds, beginning after the arc is established, during which movement of the TRAVEL axis will be inhibited. The purpose of the TRAVEL DELAY period is to establish a stable arc and a proper initial puddle of molten metal before proceeding with the remainder of the weld. When the travel delay period has elapsed, the travel axis will begin moving at the speed programmed in the active segment.

param.name: %1 START DELAY
param.desc: The duration in seconds, beginning after the arc is established, during which movement of the AVC axis will be inhibited. The purpose of the AVC DELAY period is to establish a stable arc and a proper initial puddle of molten metal before proceeding with the remainder of the weld. When the AVC delay period has elapsed, the AVC axis will begin moving at the speed programmed in the active segment.

param.name: %1 START DELAY
param.desc: The duration in seconds, beginning after the arc is established, during which wire feed will be inhibited. The purpose of the WIRE DELAY period is to establish a stable arc and a proper initial puddle of molten metal before introducing filler wire to the weld. When the wire delay period has elapsed, the wire will begin to feed at the speed programmed in the active segment.

param.name: %1 START DELAY
param.desc: Referring to the secondary wire feeder. The duration in seconds, beginning after the arc is established, during which wire feed will be inhibited. The purpose of the WIRE DELAY period is to establish a stable arc and a proper initial puddle of molten metal before introducing filler wire to the weld. When the wire delay period has elapsed, the wire will begin to feed at the speed programmed in the active segment.

param.name: PRI AMPS
param.desc: The welding current output by the power supply during the PRIMARY portion of the pulsation cycle. Generally, this is the high current, or "hot" portion of the weld. In the short circuit transfer MIG mode this represents the base welding current.

param.name: BKG AMPS
param.desc: The welding current output by the power supply during the BACKGROUND portion of the pulsation cycle. Generally, this is the low current, or "cool" portion of the weld.

param.name: PULSE FREQ
param.desc: The pulse frequency in hertz (pulses per second). PULSE FREQ establishes the rate at which the power supply will switch the output current flow between the PRI AMP level and the BKG AMP level.

param.name: PULSE WIDTH
param.desc: The percentage of time that the pulse spends in its PRIMARY cycle. For example, a value of 60 would mean that for 60 percent of the time, the cycle would be in the PRIMARY portion, and for the remaining 40 percent of the time, the cycle would be in the BACKGROUND portion. A value of 100 percent will cause the pulsation cycle to remain in PRIMARY at all times, effectively disabling pulsation.

param.name: PRI %1
param.desc: The speed at which the TRAVEL axis will move during the PRIMARY portion of the pulsation cycle.

param.name: BKG %1
param.desc: The speed at which the TRAVEL axis will move during the BACKGROUND portion of the pulsation cycle.

param.name: PRI %1
param.desc: In TIG welding this is the speed at which the wire will feed during the PRIMARY portion of the pulsation cycle. In MIG welding this is the constant speed at which the wire will feed. This parameter will only display if the selected weld head has wire feed capability.

param.name: BKG %1
param.desc: The speed at which the wire will feed during the BACKGROUND portion of the pulsation cycle. This parameter will only display if the selected weld head has wire feed capability.

param.name: PRI %1
param.desc: The speed at which the secondary wire will feed during the PRIMARY portion of the pulsation cycle. This parameter will only display if the selected weld head has a secondary wire feed capability.

param.name: BKG %1
param.desc: The speed at which the secondary wire will feed during the BACKGROUND portion of the pulsation cycle. This parameter will only display if the selected weld head has secondary wire feed capability.

param.name: MIG VOLTS
param.desc: The voltage that the system will maintain throughout a weld using the MIG 'Constant Voltage' mode. MIG is a type of welding process. Acronym for 'Metal Inert Gas' welding. Also known as GMAW welding.

param.name: PRI VOLTS
param.desc: Short for 'Primary Automatic Voltage Control'. This refers to the AVC set point not the axis on the weld head. The voltage the system will try to maintain while welding during the PRIMARY portion of the pulsation cycle. The system will maintain this voltage by moving the AVC axis up and down.

param.name: BKG VOLTS
param.desc: Short for 'Background Automatic Voltage Control'. This refers to the AVC set point not the axis on the weld head. The voltage the system will try to maintain while welding during the BACKGROUND portion of the pulsation cycle. The system will maintain this voltage by moving the AVC axis up and down.

param.name: %1 WIDTH

param.name: IN DWELL
param.desc: The duration the cross seam oscillator will pause when it has reached the inside position of the OSC WIDTH before beginning EXCURSION to the OUT DWELL position. This parameter will only display if the selected weld head has a cross seam slide or torch oscillation capability.

param.name: OUT DWELL
param.desc: The duration the cross seam oscillator will pause when it has reached the outside position of the OSC WIDTH before beginning EXCURSION to the IN DWELL position. This parameter will only display if the selected weld head has a cross seam slide or torch oscillation capability.

param.name: EXCURSION
param.desc: The duration in seconds the cross seam oscillator takes to move between the IN DWELL and OUT DWELL positions as established by OSC WIDTH. This parameter will only display if the selected weld head has a cross seam slide or torch oscillation capability.

param.name: HOTWIRE AMPS
param.desc: The amperage that the hotwire device will output when heating the wire before it is deposited onto the part through the wire feeder.

param.name: HOTWIRE 2 AMPS
param.desc: The amperage that the secondary hotwire device will output when heating the wire before it is deposited onto the part through the secondary wire feeder.

param.name: PRE PURGE
param.desc: The duration that shield gas will flow onto the work piece before the arc is initiated and the weld sequence proceeds into segment. The PREPURGE period allows the area surrounding the arc to be purged of contaminating atmosphere and the proper inert gas envelope to be established.

param.name: POST PURGE
param.desc: The duration that shield gas will flow after DOWNSLOPE has been completed and the arc has been extinguished. The POSTPURGE period allows the tungsten tip to cool down to a point at which it will remain unaffected by oxidation from surrounding atmosphere.

param.name: INITIAL AMPS
param.desc: The amount of arc current which will flow immediately after a transfer arc has been established. This occurs after IMPULSE TIME in a high frequency arc start operation or after the electrode has lifted away from the work piece in a touch start operation. This is the value that the arc current starts from when the weld sequence enters the first segment.

param.name: FINAL AMPS
param.desc: The value toward which the arc current slopes during the DOWNSLOPE period. Change this parameter to allow the arc to extinguish properly at the end of the weld.

param.name: IMPULSE AMPS
param.desc: The amount of current output by the power supply to preheat the tungsten tip and to help stabilize the arc during a high frequency arc start operation. The impulse occurs at the beginning of the high frequency arc start operation and lasts for IMPULSE TIME. At the end of IMPULSE TIME the arc current will drop to the value of the INITIAL AMPS setting. This parameter will only display if a high frequency arc starter is being used.

param.name: IMPULSE TIME
param.desc: The amount of time the impulse current will be outputted for during a high frequency arc start operation.

param.name: TRAIL GAS
param.desc: Enables/disables the gas that follows or 'trails' the torch to continue to shield and cool the weld down.

param.name: BACKUP GAS
param.desc: Enables/disables the gas that follows or 'trails' the torch to continue to shield and cool the weld down.

param.name: %1 STOP DELAY
param.desc: AVC is an acronym for 'Automatic Voltage Control'. The time period that the AVC axis will continue making corrections after the weld has completed.

param.name: %1 DEAD BAND
param.desc: The DEAD BAND is the amount of voltage error allowed before the AVC axis will respond.

param.name: %1 SLOW BAND
param.desc: The SLOW BAND is the range of voltage error where the AVC axis will respond using the LOW SENS setting.

param.name: LIFT GAP
param.desc: The distance in inches that the system will lift the electrode away from the workpiece when an arc is initiated using a TOUCH ARC. If a touch and retract start is used then this is the distance from the electrode to work at which a high frequency arc start will occur.

param.name: %1 LOW SENSITIVITY
param.desc: This is a measure of how quickly the AVC responds to changes in the arc voltage when the voltage error is inside the SLOW BAND. Increasing this number increases the sensitivity and the quickness of the response. Setting this value to 0 will disable the AVC system in the SLOW BAND.

param.name: %1 HIGH SENSITIVITY
param.desc: This is a measure of how quickly the AVC responds to changes in the arc voltage outside of the SLOW BAND. Increasing this number increases the sensitivity and the quickness of the response. Setting this value to 0 will disable the AVC system outside of the SLOW BAND.

param.desc: The duration in seconds, beginning at the start of the segment, during which the weld current will linearly increase or decrease from the PRI AMP/BKG AMP values established in the previous segment to the PRI AMP/BKG AMP values for the current segment. The slope will not continue past the current segment should the weld sequence advance to the next segment before the SLOPE TIME has elapsed. The SLOPE TIME parameter for segment 1 is also referred to as UPSLOPE time. During UPSLOPE time, the weld current will slope from the INITIAL AMPS value in the SETUP screen to the PRI AMP/BKG AMP values for segment 1.
